text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.

Brazilian exports totalled a record $47.7 billion in 1996, a slight rise of 2.67 percent over 1995. In December, Brazil exported $3.79 billion, with a daily average of $189.5 million, the worst figure since March.
Brazil's 1996 trade deficit is seen at about $5.0 billion.

The retail sector was a good investment in 1996. Easier credit and steady prices gave a boost to the sector, leading shares of retail firms Guararapes, Lojas Arapua, Pao de Acucar and Lojas Renner to rise at least 70 percent.
-- MALAN TO DECIDE ON CPMF TAX ON STOCKS

Finance Minister Pedro Malan will decide whether stock trades will be subject to the so-called CPMF tax. The government has already agreed that foreign investors under Annex Four rules will have a special treatment.
-- LEADER SEES RE-ELECTION ONLY FOR PRESIDENT

Inocencio Oliveira, Liberal Front Party (PFL) leader in the Chamber of Deputies, expects re-election to be approved only for President Fernando Henrique Cardoso. He said regional rivalries may lead the government bloc in Congress to block the re-election for state governors and mayors.
-- RAINS LEAVE 65,000 HOMELESS IN THREE STATES
Heavy rains have left at least 65,000 homeless in Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro and Espirito Santo states.
-- PPB GOES TO MALUF AND SAYS RE-ELECTION WILL BE APPROVED

Paulo Maluf's Brazilian Progressive Party (PPB), the main opponent of the re-election proposal, admits that the amendment will be approved next week. At a meeting with the party president Espiridiao Amin and deputy Delfim Netto on Tuesday, Maluf was told that only half of the 90 PPB deputies will vote against the re-election amendment.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
